ingredients.item: Water to cover; 1 tsp salt ; a splash of vinegar in the boil
/2 tsp toasted sesame oil , off heat; sesame seeds to finish

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The peeled eggs into the simmering braise, 10 minutes at the barest bubble — this first simmer drives the soy in through the warm shell-less whites.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the whites have gone from white to café-au-lait at the surface; the braise smells of soy and sweet garlic.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Off the heat, and the marinating is the recipe: the eggs sit in the braise 1 hour at room temperature, then refrigerate in their liquid overnight. The color deepens to walnut, the soy reaches the yolk's border, the flavor rounds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the next day's taste test: cut one — a marbled tan white, a bright yolk with a savory halo at its edge. The egg should taste seasoned-through, not dipped.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Serve drained, lightly wet with the braise, sesame over — and the braise itself goes back to work: it is now an egg-fragrant half-batch of jangjorim soy, ready to braise the beef (#B20) or a second round of eggs (top the liquid up with a splash of water and soy).
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test at the drinking table or in the lunchbox: one bite, the savory-sweet white snapping against the rich yolk — the bowl empties two eggs at a time per person, and that ratio is the recipe's only scaling law.

the eating test at the drinking table or in the lunchbox: one bite, the savory-sweet white snapping against the rich yolk — the bowl empties two eggs at a time per person, and that ratio is the recipe's only scaling law.
storageNotes: Keeps 4–5 days refrigerated in their liquid (the make-ahead banchan, improving daily). The spent braise gets one more career (#B20, or round two of eggs).

Variations: the jalapeño-spiced fork; chicken eggs run the same braise at a longer soak (2 days) for the marbled deviled-egg lane; the eggs halved over hot rice with a spoon of the liquid is the lunchbox's crown.
